title: Efficient greybox fuzzing framework with tabu search
task: Seed scheduling and energy allocation in fuzzing for vulnerability detection
key_results: 19.89% improvement in path exploration over AFL
160.87% improvement in crash discovery over AFL across 24-hour trials
comments: The tabu search formulation for seed scheduling is intuitive, though the comparison baselines (FairFuzz, MOPT, EcoFuzz) are somewhat dated and lack recent state-of-the-art fuzzers.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tabu search-based seed scheduling outperforms coarse-grained heuristics in identifying high-quality seeds
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TabuFuzz achieved 19.89% higher path exploration than AFL

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive energy allocation using fine-grained dynamic execution information improves crash discovery
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 160.87% improvement in crash discovery over baseline AFL

title: Specifics of the growth of lithium-doped KCl single crystals by the Bridgman method in an argon atmosphere
task: Growth and purification of lithium-doped KCl single crystals via Bridgman method
key_results: Purified KCl matrix to 0.2 ppm OH, 0.1–0.3 ppm Me²⁺, and 1–3 ppm alkali-metal impurities; enhanced scintillation and dosimetric properties demonstrated in KCl:Li crystals
comments: The argon atmosphere approach effectively suppresses halogen evaporation, though quantitative comparison with vacuum-only or alternative growth methods is not provided.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pyrolytic carbon coating suppresses adhesion of molten AHC to quartz walls
hypotheses.result: Coating successfully applied and enabled crystal growth without wall adhesion

hypotheses.hypothesis: Argon atmosphere suppresses halogen vapor evaporation
hypotheses.result: Argon at 1.1–1.3 bar maintained crystal integrity and purity levels

title: Thermal transport and crystallisation in octadecane composites with porous framework coatings and graphene
task: Thermal conductivity and crystallization control in octadecane phase-change composites with hybrid coatings and graphene
key_results: ZIF-8-coated composite: thermal conductivity 0.78 ± 0.04 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, supercooling 1.2 ± 0.2 °C; UiO-66-coated: 0.72 ± 0.03 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, 2.4 ± 0.3 °C; ZIF-8 retained 98.2 ± 1.1% melting enthalpy after 1000 thermal cycles
comments: Synergistic effect of coating and graphene on thermal transport is evident but the isolation of individual mechanisms remains incomplete; device-scale performance testing is explicitly absent.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MOF coatings and graphene additively enhance thermal transport
hypotheses.result: Neither coating nor graphene alone explains composite thermal conductivity; synergistic interaction confirmed

hypotheses.hypothesis: ZIF-8 coating reduces crystallization delay relative to UiO-66
hypotheses.result: ZIF-8 showed 1.2 °C supercooling vs. 2.4 °C for UiO-66; coating thickness and topology may influence nucleation
